text:
mari: FYI customer ACME (zendesk #9876) reports huge embeddings bill and weird latency spikes starting yesterday. They say cache hit rate dropped to ~2%.
mari: they attached request example + response showing dimension mismatch for some items.
ash: can you paste the request/response snippet?
mari: customer snippet:
```json
{"model":"embed-large-v2","input":"Product description...","tenant_id":"acme-prod","embedding_dim":1536}
```
mari: response includes embedding vector length 768 for ~3 out of 10 items, plus empty cache hits.
koji: 768 vs 1536 suggests mixed model variants or quantized model serving. Did they pin model version?
mari: they did: model set to `embed-large-v2@2025-11-01`. They also say they send batched requests of 16 items, sometimes get 200ms, sometimes 1.2s.
sam: any recent config change on cache key formatting? I remember a rollout of multi-namespace keys last week.
ash: yes — we shipped namespace prefix change (internal ref: CACHE-KEY-2025-11). It prepends `ns:{tenant}` for new keys but retains old read path for backward compat only for non-batched lookups. I did not think about batched cache key hashing.
mari: customer claims behavior is nondeterministic: same payload sometimes hits, sometimes misses. They saw duplicate upstream calls — duplicate generation attempts in the logs.
emb-cache-bot: debug log: batch_id=bbf9 key_list=["ns:acme-prod|embed-large-v2|h:0x1a2b","embed-large-v2|h:0x1a2b", "ns:acme-prod|embed-large-v2|h:0x2f3c"] - hit_flags=[false,false,false] - fallback_candidates=["embed-large-v2|h:0x1a2b"]
koji: hm the mixed keys look like some items in the batch are being prefixed and some are not. That would cause a miss and then fallback to uncached generation causing latency and extra billing.
ash: possible race: some worker pool running old binary that emits legacy keys into batch. We partially rolled across AZs.
mari: customer billing shows ~3x token charges for embeddings calls during window. They want credit + root cause.
sam: reproduce steps I ran locally: send 4 identical inputs in a single batch, hit rate fluctuates if you mix pipelined requests across threads. Repro snippet:
```bash
for i in 1 2 3 4; do curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings \
  -d '{"model":"embed-large-v2","input":["test string","test string"]}' &
done
wait
```
ash: logs show worker A (old) produced keys without `ns:` for items processed in same batch as worker B (new). The cache service treats the key list atomically for batch lookup but our serializer wasn't normalizing keys before the atomic check.
koji: that explains dimension mismatch too: if a batch mix routes to different model variants (quantized vs full precision) because of fallback routing, some items can be served by a different model, hence 768 vector.
mari: customer asked whether auth/tenant scoping could have leaked keys across tenants. Any evidence?
ash: no cross-tenant hits observed. Old key format lacked explicit tenant prefix but contained tenant_id hashed into `h:` . Collision unlikely but possible to get different model variant for same hash if routing differs. But logs show `ns:acme-prod` keys were present alongside legacy keys for same batch.
billing-bot: found billing spike: 2025-11-20T03:00-04:00 window, embeddings token_count=1.9M (baseline 700k). Extra cost mainly from fallback_gen calls logged as `gen_v2_fallback`.
sam: mitigation plan: 1) force all workers to run new serializer (hotfix) 2) add normalization step before batch cache lookup 3) backfill detection to map legacy keys to new keys for a short migration period.
koji: also add a check when serving embeddings: if returned vector length != expected model dim, log and route to fallback silently instead of returning mismatched vector. That prevents corrupt results.
mari: customer asked for immediate workaround on their side — suggested pinning to a specific non-rollout model variant?
koji: yes pin to `embed-large-v2@2025-09-10-stable` which we guarantee has consistent dim 1536 and no migration naming. But that won't fix billing.
ash: I pushed hotfix tag `cache-serializer-20251120` to all pools; rolling out now. I'll monitor cache hit rate.
emb-cache-bot: post-fix report (10m sample): hit_rate increased from 2% -> 78% for ACME tenant; duplicate generation events decreased by 92%.
mari: customer confirmed lower latency and much lower cost during test window. They requested an invoice credit for the spike.
sam: recommend credit of amount equal to delta in embeddings generation requests (~1.2M tokens). I'll file formal credit request to finance.
mari: action items:
- ash to complete rollout and add normalization guard (ETA 2h)
- koji to add dim-check and silent-fallback (ETA 1 day)
- sam to open finance credit (done: FIN-REQ-4312)
- mari to update customer with RCA and timeline (in progress)
ash: I'll attach PR and logs to the ticket. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving/pull/789
koji: follow-up: we should add unit test for batched key normalization + a canary job to validate caching behavior across mixed-version workers.
mari: customer reply: "thanks — latency much better and bill looks normal in our staging test. Please confirm final RCA & credit timeline."
mari: marking for postmortem if billing credit > $5k.
ash: logging note: we found no evidence of tenant data leakage. Root cause: rolling rollout introduced mixed cache key formats in batched serializer which caused atomic batch misses and fallback generation, causing extra token generation and occasional model variant fallthrough.
koji: closing loop: once dim-check in place, we'll run a backfill to detect any items that got served with wrong dims and notify affected customers.
mari: closing thread for now, will reopen if ACME sees further issues. :thumbsup:
